mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE drops > 0.5% in 1 month and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over a 3-month period signals increased demand for housing and related goods, which boosts economic activity and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases over a 3-month period and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in one month signals a contraction in supply, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If INDPRO drops > 1% in 1 month and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the Consumer Price Index (CPI) is rising, the interaction signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL is rising, but S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases, the interaction signals a robust labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases, but S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Real Gross Domestic Product (GDPC1) growth above 2.5% in a quarter signals strong economic demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth > 2.5% in a quarter and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in a month signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS drops > 0.25% in 1 month and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.
